page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.small is an arm64-based virtual machine instance powered by a single dedicated core of an Alibaba Yitian710 processor running at 2.75 GHz. It features 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1776.78 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1375.0. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds registering at 21.07 GB/sec and 8.2 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and database operations show poor relative performance, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 1076.73 and a Redis SET throughput of 1.68 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g8y.small offers a low-cost entry point into the Arm64 ecosystem, utilizing custom silicon to deliver dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of multi-threaded virtualization. Due to its single-core limitation and lack of local storage, it is not suited for parallel processing, heavy database workloads, or memory-intensive applications. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, development and testing environments, or simple background microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.small is an arm64-based instance configured with 1 dedicated vCPU and 4.0 GB of memory. Powered by an Alibaba Yitian710 processor running at 2.75 GHz, this KVM-based server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network. Performance benchmarks reveal average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1375.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1776.78. However, its single-core architecture results in poor multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, with uncached memory write speeds limited to 8.2 GB/sec. This instance provides a cost-efficient entry point for Arm64 development but presents clear tradeoffs in parallel processing and database throughput. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, and microservices.
